questions.title: Welcome Banner
questions.objective: Print fixed-width border lines using string multiplication and centered text.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: An automated onboarding terminal displays a personalized greeting banner for incoming engineering students.

The banner is enclosed by top and bottom borders made of exactly 40 equal signs (`=`). The center line begins and ends with a vertical bar (`|`), with the inner greeting message centered within the remaining 38 characters (`msg.center(38)`):
Line 1: 40 '=' characters
Line 2: | + centered 'Welcome, <name>!' across 38 spaces + |
Line 3: 40 '=' characters

Given the student's name from standard input, print the 3-line welcome banner.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the student's name (string).
questions.output_format: Three lines forming the fixed 40-character wide banner.
hints: Construct the border line using '=' * 40.
Create the inner text msg = f'Welcome, {name}!' and center it using msg.center(38).
Wrap the centered content in vertical bars: f'|{msg.center(38)}|'.
questions.reference_solution:
name = input().strip()
msg = f"Welcome, {name}!"
border = "=" * 40
print(border)
print(f"|{msg.center(38)}|")
print(border)

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing the student's name (string).
extra_fields.output_format: Three lines forming the fixed 40-character wide banner.

questions.title: ASCII Hackathon Badge
questions.objective: Read 3 lines and format a bordered participant card using +, -, |.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: At an inter-college hackathon, registration staff print rectangular identification badges. The badge has a fixed width of exactly 32 characters.

The layout consists of:
Top & Bottom Borders: '+' followed by 30 '-' characters and ending with '+' (width 32)
Inner Lines (each width 32):
- '| Name: ' followed by name left-aligned to 21 characters and ' |'
- '| Team: ' followed by team left-aligned to 21 characters and ' |'
- '| Track: ' followed by track left-aligned to 21 characters and ' |'

Given three separate lines containing name, team, and track respectively, print the 5-line badge.
questions.input_format:
Three separate lines:
Line 1: Name
Line 2: Team Name
Line 3: Track Name
questions.output_format: Five lines displaying the 32-character wide badge.
hints: Read input line by line using input().strip().
Use f-string formatting with width specifiers: {name:<21}.
Verify that every line, including borders, is exactly 32 characters long.
questions.reference_solution:
name = input().strip()
team = input().strip()
track = input().strip()
border = "+" + "-" * 30 + "+"
print(border)
print(f"| Name:  {name:<21} |")
print(f"| Team:  {team:<21} |")
print(f"| Track: {track:<21} |")
print(border)

questions.title: Bill Split Calculation
questions.objective: Read total bill, tip percentage, and head count; output per-person share to 2 decimal places.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Friends dining at a restaurant split their total bill evenly. They calculate the tip based on the base bill, add it to the total, and then divide the final sum among the number of people.

Formulas:
- `total_with_tip = bill * (1.0 + tip_pct / 100.0)`
- `share = total_with_tip / people`

Given bill, tip_pct, and people as space-separated numbers on a single line, calculate and print each person's payable share in the format: `Per Person: Rs. <share:.2f>`.
questions.input_format: A single line containing bill (float), tip_pct (float), and people (int) separated by spaces.
questions.output_format: A single line: Per Person: Rs. <share:.2f>
hints: Convert inputs using bill = float(parts[0]), tip = float(parts[1]), people = int(parts[2]).
Calculate total = bill * (1 + tip / 100), then share = total / people.
Format the output with two decimal places using {share:.2f}.
questions.reference_solution:
bill_str, tip_str, people_str = input().split()
bill = float(bill_str)
tip_pct = float(tip_str)
people = int(people_str)
total = bill * (1.0 + tip_pct / 100.0)
share = total / people
print(f"Per Person: Rs. {share:.2f}")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing bill (float), tip_pct (float), and people (int) separated by spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: A single line: Per Person: Rs. <share:.2f>

questions.title: Pizza Crust vs Cheese Area
questions.objective: Calculate inner cheese area and outer crust ring area using pi = 3.14159 to 2 decimal places.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A pizzeria menu application displays the breakdown between the inner cheese surface area and the outer crust ring area.

Formulas (using pi = 3.14159):
- Outer radius: `R = diameter / 2.0`
- Inner radius: `r = R - crust_width`
- Cheese area: `pi * (r ** 2)`
- Crust ring area: `pi * (R ** 2 - r ** 2)`

Given diameter and crust_width as space-separated floats on a single line, calculate and display both areas to 2 decimal places.
questions.input_format: A single line containing diameter and crust_width (floats in cm) separated by a space.
questions.output_format: A single line: Cheese Area: <cheese:.2f> sq cm | Crust Area: <crust:.2f> sq cm
sample_outputs: Cheese Area: 490.87 sq cm | Crust Area: 215.98 sq cm
Cheese Area: 201.06 sq cm | Crust Area: 113.10 sq cm
hints: Use the exact approved value PI = 3.14159.
Compute outer radius R = diameter / 2.0 and inner radius r = R - crust_width.
Format both results to 2 decimal places: {:.2f}.
questions.reference_solution:
PI = 3.14159
d_s, c_s = input().split()
diameter = float(d_s)
crust = float(c_s)
R = diameter / 2.0
r = R - crust
cheese_area = PI * (r ** 2)
crust_area = PI * (R ** 2 - r ** 2)
print(f"Cheese Area: {cheese_area:.2f} sq cm | Crust Area: {crust_area:.2f} sq cm")

questions.title: Quick-Commerce Receipt
questions.objective: Read 3 item lines (name, qty, unit price), sum totals, add delivery fee, and print aligned receipt.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: An on-demand grocery delivery service generates an aligned ASCII receipt for an order of 3 distinct items with a fixed delivery fee of Rs. 30.00.

Input consists of 3 lines, each containing:
`<ItemName> <Quantity> <UnitPrice>`

Receipt Layout (width exactly 34 characters):
`+--------------------------------+`
`| Item Qty Total |`
`|--------------------------------|`
For each item:
`| {name:<14} {qty:>4} {subtotal:>10.2f} |`
`|--------------------------------|`
`| Delivery Fee: 30.00 |`
`| Total: {grand_total:>11.2f} |`
`+--------------------------------+`

Note: The 'Total' column displays the subtotal for that item (Quantity * UnitPrice).
questions.input_format: Three lines, each containing ItemName (string <= 14 chars), Quantity (int), and UnitPrice (float) separated by spaces.
hints: Read all 3 items and calculate subtotal = qty * unit_price.
Sum all 3 subtotals and add 30.00 for grand_total.
Format each item with f'| {name:<14} {qty:>4} {subtotal:>10.2f} |'.
questions.reference_solution:
items = []
sub_total = 0.0
for _ in range(3):
    name, q_s, p_s = input().split()
    qty = int(q_s)
    price = float(p_s)
    sub = qty * price
    sub_total += sub
    items.append((name, qty, sub))

grand_total = sub_total + 30.00
border = "+--------------------------------+"
div = "|--------------------------------|"

print(border)
print("| Item             Qty     Total |")
print(div)
for name, qty, sub in items:
    print(f"| {name:<14} {qty:>4} {sub:>10.2f} |")
print(div)
print(f"| Delivery Fee:            30.00 |")
print(f"| Total:             {grand_total:>11.2f} |")
print(border)

extra_fields.input_format: Three lines, each containing ItemName (string <= 14 chars), Quantity (int), and UnitPrice (float) separated by spaces.

questions.title: Product Discount Summary
questions.objective: Calculate integer discount percentage from MRP and sale price, and print a formatted summary card.
questions.problem_statement:

Formulas:
- Discount amount: `discount_amount = mrp - sale_price`
- Discount percentage (round half up): `discount_pct = int(((discount_amount / mrp) * 100) + 0.5)`. Do not use Python's round(), because it rounds exact .5 values to the nearest even number.

Layout (width 28 characters):
`****************************`
`* MRP: Rs. {mrp:>8.2f} *`
`* Sale Price: Rs. {sale:>8.2f} *`
`* Discount: {discount_pct:>3}% *`
`****************************`

Given MRP and sale_price on a single line, print the 5-line summary card.
questions.input_format: A single line containing MRP and sale_price (floats) separated by a space.
questions.output_format: Five lines displaying the 28-character wide discount card.
hints: Compute discount_pct = int(((mrp - sale) / mrp) * 100 + 0.5).
Use border = '*' * 28.
Format prices with {x:>8.2f} and the discount with {discount_pct:>3} followed by a literal % sign (do not use the % format specifier).
questions.reference_solution:
mrp_s, sale_s = input().split()
mrp = float(mrp_s)
sale = float(sale_s)
discount_pct = int(((mrp - sale) / mrp) * 100 + 0.5)
border = "*" * 28

print(border)
print(f"* MRP:        Rs. {mrp:>8.2f} *")
print(f"* Sale Price: Rs. {sale:>8.2f} *")
print(f"* Discount:           {discount_pct:>3}% *")

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing MRP and sale_price (floats) separated by a space.
extra_fields.output_format: Five lines displaying the 28-character wide discount card.

- Storage: Rs. 0.50 per GB (`storage_gb * 0.50`)
- Bandwidth: First 50.0 GB is free; excess bandwidth is billed at Rs. 2.00 per GB (`max(0.0, bandwidth - 50.0) * 2.00`)

questions.title: Bitcoin to Satoshi Converter
questions.objective: Convert a decimal BTC amount to integer Satoshis (10^8) using exact decimal arithmetic with comma separators.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Cryptocurrency wallet engines convert high-level Bitcoin (BTC) balances into integer Satoshis without binary floating-point roundoff error:
`1 BTC = 100,000,000 Satoshis`

To avoid IEEE 754 precision issues (e.g. `0.00523 * 100000000` producing inaccurate binary fractions), parse the input using `decimal.Decimal`.

Output format:
`<sats:,> satoshis` (or `<sats:,> satoshi` if exactly 1 satoshi).

Given the BTC amount as a string, print the formatted satoshi count.
questions.input_format: A single line containing the BTC amount as a decimal string.
questions.output_format: A single line: <sats:,> satoshis (or 1 satoshi if exactly 1).
hints: Use from decimal import Decimal to avoid float precision issues.
Convert to satoshis: sats = int(Decimal(input().strip()) * 100_000_000).
Handle singular vs plural: unit = 'satoshi' if sats == 1 else 'satoshis'.
questions.reference_solution:
from decimal import Decimal
btc_str = input().strip()
sats = int(Decimal(btc_str) * 100000000)
unit = "satoshi" if sats == 1 else "satoshis"
print(f"{sats:,} {unit}")

questions.title: Daily Freelancer Earnings
questions.objective: Calculate total pay and 10% TDS deduction across 3 project lines with 2-decimal alignment.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A freelance invoicing aggregator computes gross pay, statutory tax deduction at source (10% TDS), and net payout across 3 daily project milestones.

Input consists of 3 lines, each containing:
`<ProjectName> <Hours> <HourlyRate>`
(Note: Project names may contain spaces; Hours and HourlyRate are the last two space-separated numeric tokens).

Formulas:
- For each project: `pay = hours * hourly_rate`
- `gross = sum(pay)`
- `tds = gross * 0.10`
- `net = gross - tds`

Output format:
`Gross Earnings: Rs. <gross:.2f>`
`TDS Deduction (10%): Rs. <tds:.2f>`
`Net Payable: Rs. <net:.2f>`
questions.input_format: Three lines, each containing ProjectName (string), Hours (float), and HourlyRate (float).
questions.output_format: Three lines displaying Gross Earnings, TDS Deduction (10%), and Net Payable.
sample_outputs:
Gross Earnings: Rs. 9750.00
TDS Deduction (10%): Rs. 975.00
Net Payable: Rs. 8775.00

Gross Earnings: Rs. 7750.00
TDS Deduction (10%): Rs. 775.00
Net Payable: Rs. 6975.00
hints: Parse each line using line.rsplit(maxsplit=2) to support multi-word project names.
Multiply hours * rate for each project and accumulate gross earnings.
Compute tds = gross * 0.10 and net = gross - tds, formatting each with :.2f.
questions.reference_solution:
gross = 0.0
for _ in range(3):
    parts = input().strip().rsplit(maxsplit=2)
    h = float(parts[1])
    r = float(parts[2])
    gross += h * r

tds = gross * 0.10
net = gross - tds
print(f"Gross Earnings: Rs. {gross:.2f}")
print(f"TDS Deduction (10%): Rs. {tds:.2f}")
print(f"Net Payable: Rs. {net:.2f}")
